summary: Roxy Ann Peak lookout above Medford, OR: 15-foot pole platform and cabin dated to 1941, now gone; summit now has a 2007 radio tower.

facts.status_note: Register and firelookout.com say the platform and cabin are gone; no removal date given

access.note: Summit lies inside Prescott Park, a city park; Wikipedia describes road access to the summit (Roxy Ann Road, then Tower Road)

events.note: Morning Oregonian report dated October 6, 1933 of city plans for Roxy Ann park, including a lookout tower among other buildings; not shown as built
Register build year for a 15-foot pole platform and cabin
180-foot radio tower built on the summit, replacing three of four 80-foot towers; no source ties it to the lookout

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and firelookout.com name the Oregon Dept. of Forestry; the Forest Lookouts page heads its entry with the City of Medford. Both are recorded; neither is chosen.
A 1933 plan mentions a lookout tower among park buildings, while the register dates the platform and cabin to 1941. The sources do not say whether they are the same structure.

notes_for_editor: No staffing, fire or removal-date sources found. Agency conflict (ODF vs City of Medford) and 1933 plan vs 1941 build are both reported in the story. Access is set to public from Wikipedia's description of Prescott Park as a city park and its road access to the summit; no source describes the lookout site itself. The 2007 radio tower is not linked to the lookout by any source. The LivingNewDeal page returned 403 and the Medford city park page returned almost no text, so neither was quoted.
